page.layout: One block of verse, one printed page, with a running head at the top and the page number at the top right. Verse lines are set in stanzas, indented in places. No notes in the margins, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.p:
Nuper coegit fontibus abditis
Haurire lymphas, hîc benigna
Facta Patris celebrate summi.

Quum turba portis conueniet frequens,
O nuda murus oppida, dicite
Qua dextra vindex præpotente
Cœlituum facit vsque nutu.

Iam surge vates Debora, Barbiton
Et tende: dulci dic, age, tibia
Versus canoros: atque Iouæ
Perpetuum meditare carmen.

Tuque, o, decorum laurea verticem
Barace victrix cui tegit, hostium
Duces cathenatos triumpha:
Magnus & eximias reclude
Victor. Supremi namque benignitas
Nos vera Patris robore brachij
Vult liberatos subiugata
Principibus dare iura plebis.

Me me superbo prouidus agmini
Præponit author Cœlituum Deus:
Robusta quum dat Gentis Abrae
Corda meis moderanda iussis.

Hac Gens beati pascua collibus
Ephraimitæ pinguibus incolit
Vicina, fœcundosque iungit
Dire tuis Amaleke fines.

page.notes: Text is in roman with some italic words; the printed line breaks are shown as line breaks within each stanza. Doubtful readings: "Cœlituum" in the fourth stanza is clear; "Hanc prompta bello Bengemini Tribus" is the last line of the page, read as printed. The page has ornamental flourishes (decorated initial letters, e.g. "Q", "M", "T", "N") that are read as ordinary capitals. Word "Iouæ" and "Ephraimitæ" are read from the scan but are only moderately clear. Ink damage and fold-shadow on the left edge; a slight stain near "Duces" and "Victor" which does not hide the text.
